Disclosure to Promote the Right To Information 

Whereas the Parliament of India has set out to provide a practical regime of right to 
information for citizens to secure access to information under the control of public authorities, 
in order to promote transparency and accountability in the working of every public authority, 
and whereas the attached publication of the Bureau of Indian Standards is of particular interest 
to the public, particularly disadvantaged communities and those engaged in the pursuit of 
education and knowledge, the attached public safety standard is made available to promote the 
timely dissemination of this information in an accurate manner to the public.

FOREWORD 

This Indian Standard was adopted by the Bureau of Indian Standards on 15 November 1989, after 
the draft finaliied by the Wool and Wool Products Sectional Committee had been approved by the 
Textiic Djvisjon Council. 

The worsted shawls (both all wool and blended with man-made fibres) are a widely used consumer 
Item within the country. It is hoped that the publication of this standard would ensure the 
availability of worsted shawls of required quality to the consumers 

For the purpose of deciding whether a particular Tequirement of this standard is complied with, the 
final value, observed or caJcuIated* expressing the result of a test or analysis, shall be rounded off in 
accordance with IS 2 : 1960 'Rules for rounding off numencal values ( revtsedy. The number of 
significant places retained in the rounded off value should be the same as that of the specified value 
in this standard.

Indian Standard 



WORSTED SHAWLS — SPECIFICATION 



1 SCOPE 

1.1 This standard prescribes the requirements of 
worsted shawls. 

2 REFERENCES 

2.1 The Indian Standards listed in Annex \ are 
nt;cessary adjuncts to this stdndard. 

3 TERMINOLOGY 

3.0 For the purpose of this stnndard, the follo- 
wing definitions alone with thaye given in 
IS 11206 ; J 984 shall apply. 

3.1 Worsted Shawls 

Shawls made from ^^^in wool or their blends 
with man-made fibr^js spun on ^jombej fibre 
sprnnmg system. 

3.2 Worsted Spun Yarn 

Yarn spun horn long wool fibre shvers after 
removal of short fibres on the rectihner or noble 
comb and drawjjig through gjll bo-^es, 

3.3 Worsted Blended Spun Yarn 

Yarn spun from long fibre shvertjs after remo- 
val of short fibres in the combmg process. 

3.4 Virgin Wool 

Pure and new wool. Commercially it means 
wool that has not been processed or used before 
and IS thus distinctly different from re-processed 
or Tc-uscd wool. 



4 MANUFACTLfRE 

4,1 Yarn used in the manuf.Jctiire 
spun from vjrgm woo! or 



in the manutjctiire of shawls 
shall be spun from vjrgm woo! or from the 
bleud^i of wool and man-made fibres on combed 
fibre spinning system. The inin-mtide librcs to 
be used for blendjng with wool and the blend 
composition shall be as agreed between the 
buyer and the seller. 

5 REQUIREMENTS 

5.1 Freedom from Defects 

The worsted shawls whi;n visually exarnmed both 
against light and on a flat surface shall be tree 
fiom objectionable flaws. The objectionable 
flaws shall be those which immediately strike the 
eyes of the person examining the shawls and 
shall include: 

a) Missing ends and picks; 

b) Floats; 

c) Stams; 

d) Weft birs and warp section marks; 



e) Big slubs, knots and specks unless they 
are a part of the design; 

f) Prominently noticeable thick and thin 

places, 

g) Cuts and holes; and 

h) Dyeing defects ( streaks, patches, etc). 

5.2 The shawls shall meet Che requirements as 
given in Table J , 

5,2.1 Construction particulars of one popular 
variety of all wool shawls are given in Annex B 
for information only. 

6 MARKING 

6.1 The shawls shall be macked wiLb the follow- 
ing: 

a> Name of the material, 

b) The words ^Ail Wool' 'Blended Wool' or 
Tart Wool' as the case may be ( see 
Note ). 

c) Indication of the source of manufacture^ 
d> V^af of manufaQiiirc, and 

e) Length and width 

NOTE — Tn case of blended wool or part wool 
shdwl>, the b/ernJ ggmpoaition shaJf afso be indi- 
cated 111 accordance wilh IS 1793 . 1973. 

6.1.1 The shawls may also be marked with the 
Standard Mark. 

7 PACKING 

7.1 Bale Packing 

Each shawl shall be wrapped with low density 
polyethylene film of minimum 40 micron thick- 
ness and conforming to IS 250S : 1984 A suit- 
able number of such shawls shall again be cover- 
ed with another layer of polyethylene film of 
the same type followed by a water- proof packing 
paper conforming to IS 1398 : 19S2 And then be 
enclosed m an outer layer of hessian cloth/HDPE 
woven fabric, preferably conformmgto Type I of 
IS 2HfH { Part 2) : ]97l, IS 6S99 ; 1984 m the 
form of a bale. The bale shall then be strapped 
with metallic/synthetic straps. 

7.2 Case Packing 

Each shawl shall be wrapped wuh low density 
polyethylene film of minimunri 40 micron thicks 
ness and conforming to IS 2508 : 19S4 A suit- 
able number of such shawls shall then be cover-^ 
ed with a layer of kraft paper preferably con- 
forming to IS 1397 : 1967 followed by another 
layer of waterproof packing paper conforming 
to 1399 -, 1982 and then packed ii\ wooden case 
which shall be finally strapped with metallic 
sirips.

Standard Mark 

The use of the Standard Mark is governed by the provisions of the Bureau of Indian 
Standards Act, 1986 and the Rules and Regulations made thereunder. The Standard Mark on 
products covered by an Indian Standard conveys the assurance that they have been produced 
to comply with the requirements of that standard under a well defined system of inspection, 
testing and quaJity control which is devised and supervised by BIS and operated by the pro- 
ducer. Standard marked products are also continuously checked by BIS for conformity to 
that standard as a further safeguard. Details of conditions under which a licence for the use 
of the Standard Mark may be granted to manufacturers or producers may be obtained from 
the Bureau of Indian Standards.

promote harmonious development of the activities of standardization, marking and quality 
certification of goods and attending to connected matters in the country.
